references.text: Machir was a son of Manasseh and the ancestor of the Machirites, who are mentioned in the Song of Deborah as one of the tribes that took part in the battle.
The descendants of Machir and their territory, showing the connection to the tribe of Manasseh mentioned in the Song of Deborah.
Machir as a son of Manasseh, and his link to Gilead, relevant for understanding the tribes in the Song of Deborah.
Zebulun is mentioned again here in the Song of Deborah as a tribe that was willing to risk their lives in battle.
Amalek as the ancestor of the Amalekites, the enemy that Ephraim fought against according to the verse.
Israel's first battle against Amalek, which provides background for the reference to Ephraim's fight against Amalek in the Song of Deborah.
The territory of the tribe of Ephraim and their position among the tribes of Israel, relevant to their role in the Song of Deborah.
The context of the battle where Zebulun and other tribes were gathered for combat under Barak and Deborah.
